title_english: Chitou Thai Khamyang Buranji: The Historical Chronicle of the Nora Clans
description: The definitive historical chronicle of the Tai Khamyang (Nora) people compiled by Chaimet Bailung in 2008 from palm-leaf puthis and oral genealogies, detailing the migrations from Mungkong across the Patkai, royal interactions with the Ahom court, and settlement of Powaimukh and Chalapather.

full_translation: The noble Nora (Khamyang) clan departed from the ancient realm of Mungkong and crossed the high Patkai. The Ahom monarchs revered the Nora as masters of sacred script and invited their scholars to the capital of Garhgaon. The Nora priests were renowned for their mastery of sacred Lik scriptures, astronomy, and calendrical science. Our forefathers cleared the dense bamboo groves and established the settlement of Powaimukh along the Buridihing. Because wild rattan (Waai) flourished abundantly along the river mouth, they named it Maan Paa Waai. The villagers cultivated fertile lowland paddy, irrigating their fields with the cool mountain waters of Nam Jin. They erected a magnificent wooden monastery (Kyawng) where youth learned the ancient Lik Tai alphabet. The compassionate teachings of the Lord Buddha took deep root in the soul of every Tai Khamyang family. Swargadeo Rajeshwar Singha and Gaurinath Singha granted royal lands and copper plates in honor of Nora loyalty. The ancient exogamous lineages of Thomung, Chowlik, and Bailung faithfully preserved these historical records. Let not the sacred language of the Tai Nora ever perish from the earth! This Buranji chronicle stands as an immovable pillar of Tai Khamyang identity and pride.
